issue.title: Reclaim apollo root disk and stop SASE build scratch from refilling it
issue.description: apollo's root filesystem regains roughly 100G of free space without disturbing running agents, and per-launch cargo targets plus per-checkout pytest scratch are reclaimed automatically so the disk does not refill.

issue.title: Emergency reclaim on apollo
issue.description: apollo-emergency-reclaim: over ssh with no repo changes, delete finished agents' cargo targets, stale zorg target dirs, trashed pre-cutover SASE trees, stale pytest scratch, and legacy cargo strays, with liveness guards and before/after df accounting.

issue.title: Runner-exit scratch cleanup and low-free-space pressure reaping
issue.description: agent-scratch-exit-cleanup: remove the runner's launch-assigned cargo-targets and agent-tmp directories at exit, and use a 1h pressure min age whenever the free-space floor is breached regardless of which pressure trigger fired, with tests.

issue.title: Reap sibling pytest scratch roots
issue.description: pytest-scratch-sibling-reap: make tools/run_pytest also reap stale runs in other /var/tmp/sase-<sha8> roots owned by the user and remove empty stale roots, with tests.

payload.entry: PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: ~146M remains in ~/.local/share/Trash/files/_cacache on apollo, owned by root (files are -r--r--r-- root:root inside a root-owned directory). bryan has no passwordless sudo so this cannot be removed as part of this phase; needs a sudo-capable pass or an owner audit of how root-owned files ended up in bryans npm trash.

Emergency reclaim done over ssh apollo, no repo changes. df -h / went from 9.3G to 110G available (target was 80G). Steps: (1) deleted dead entries under ~/.cache/sase/tmp/{cargo-targets,agent-tmp} after a liveness scan of every bryan-owned process's environ/cwd/fd plus a 30m mtime check, keeping all launches with a live CARGO_TARGET_DIR/TMPDIR match (~19G freed). (2) permanently deleted Trash sase-org, sase_1, and most of _cacache after confirming each .trashinfo Path/DeletionDate (~49G freed; ~146M of _cacache left behind, root-owned, noted as follow-up). (3) rm -rf'd target/ in zorg_100, zorg_101, zorg_102, and the primary zorg checkout after confirming no process cwd was under zettel-org (~29G freed). (4) reaped stale (>2h, no live .lock) pytest-<N>/garbage-* run dirs under every /var/tmp/sase-<hash> root, then removed orphan root sase-5d01d5fa entirely after confirming its checkout hash matched none of the current workspaces/sase-org/sase-core checkouts and nothing in it predated the 12h window (~1G+ freed). (5) rm -rf'd the legacy ~/tmp/sase/cargo-targets stray after confirming no live env/cwd/recent-mtime match (~1.8G freed). Step 6 (uv/npm cache prune) was skipped since free space already exceeded 60G well before reaching it. Verified after: the run_agent_runner.py PIDs seen at the start of the sweep are still alive except three that finished normally during the sweep, and 'sase disk list' runs cleanly. No --epic-symbol entries for this bead.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: Symvision cannot see monitor store module-attribute consumers — just check fails on public monitor_records/project_records in src/sase/monitor/store.py even though src/sase/monitor/store_lane.py consumes them via the store module to preserve monkeypatchability.

Implemented default-only sibling pytest scratch reaping. Verified focused module with .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_run_pytest_tmpdir.py (19 passed). Ran just check; it passed fmt, ruff, mypy, feature flags, pyscripts, test waits, changelog, and terminology, then failed unrelated symvision monitor_records/project_records; PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP noted on this bead. epic-symbols reported none.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: unrelated full-suite verification failures after core-identity escalation — investigate shell substrate stale monitor/start.py audit, gate singleton mount ordering, AF_UNIX socket path length under long workspaces, unquoted sys.executable in commit-hook test, and /tmp symlink path expectation on macOS.

Implemented runner-exit managed scratch cleanup and low-free-space pressure age change. Verified: .venv/bin/python tools/run_pytest fast tests/test_managed_tmp_reaper.py tests/test_run_agent_runner_scratch_cleanup.py tests/test_axe_chop_output_contract.py::test_managed_tmp_reap_emits_noop_summary tests/test_axe_chop_output_contract.py::test_managed_tmp_reap_emits_action_summary tests/test_agent_artifact_directory_operation_audit.py::test_artifact_directory_operation_sites_are_reviewed (42 passed); targeted stale audit/terminology rerun (6 passed); just fmt-py-check; just _lint-ruff; just _lint-symvision. Also ran just check: lint gates passed, then test-scoped escalated to full suite due core-identity-changed and failed unrelated tests recorded as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP.

Reopening: this phase was closed as done, but its changes did not reach master. There is no landed commit referencing sase-10r.2, and commit 6a60ee5fb7 from sase-zw.8.1 replaced the Python reaper implementation that the original phase edited. This turn is completing the phase by putting the low-free-space pressure min-age rule in the Rust managed-tmp owner and adding liveness-guarded runner-exit cleanup for launch-assigned scratch.

Completed the previously-missing phase work. Landed liveness-guarded runner-exit cleanup for launch-assigned managed scratch: launches export SASE_LAUNCH_SCRATCH_KEY; runner cleanup removes only matching cargo-targets/<key> and agent-tmp/<key> direct children, skips monitor/gate handoffs and missing procfs, keeps both trees if any live same-uid procfs environ/cwd reference remains, and never raises. Landed Rust-owned managed-tmp low-free-space pressure age: additive request field pressure_low_free_space_min_age_seconds, config managed_tmp.pressure.low_free_space_min_age_seconds default 3600, effective pressure age min(base, low-space) whenever the free-space floor is breached, result field pressure_effective_min_age_seconds, and chop summary pressure_min_age_seconds. Python remains a thin adapter. Docs/schema/default_config/tests updated. Verification: just install passed; core focused cargo test -p sase_core managed_tmp passed (17 managed_tmp tests); focused Python run passed (106 passed). Core just check is blocked by unrelated clippy::too_many_arguments in crates/sase_core/src/procs/runtime.rs:evaluate_candidate; main just check is blocked by unrelated Symvision findings continuation_protected_dirs and iter_ace_run_month_dirs after earlier gates passed; both routed to active Green CI epic sase-10w. sase-core-revision.txt intentionally not edited; normal ratchet-core-revision flow is still pending after the core commit publishes.

All three phases are now complete. Phase 1 performed the apollo emergency reclaim over SSH with no repo changes; apollo / is currently 193G size, 90G used, 104G available (47%). Phase 2 was corrected in this turn after the earlier false close: runner-exit scratch cleanup now removes only launch-owned scratch when procfs liveness says nothing still uses it, and the Rust managed-tmp owner applies the 1h low-free-space pressure age through an additive wire/config field while reporting the effective age. Phase 3 sibling pytest scratch reaping was already landed. Follow-up dispositions: the remaining ~146M root-owned apollo Trash _cacache residue is a one-off sudo/host-ownership issue, not SASE product work, so no task bead was created. The old phase-2 full-suite failures were either already represented by existing tasks (for example sase-10p for monitor/start.py, sase-wt for sys.executable-with-space shebangs, and closed sase-w6 for macOS /tmp symlink expectations) or were not reproduced by this turn's focused/current verification before unrelated lint gates stopped just check. The phase-3 monitor_records/project_records Symvision issue already exists as task sase-10q. Today's unrelated core clippy and main Symvision gate failures were routed to active Green CI epic sase-10w. Coordination notes were added to sase-zw.8.5 and sase-zw.8 so their pressure-contract work preserves pressure_low_free_space_min_age_seconds and pressure_effective_min_age_seconds. sase-core-revision.txt still needs the normal ratchet after the core commit publishes.
